subject: math.CT
name: Yoneda lemma
statement: For a locally small category C, a functor F:C to Set, and an object A, natural transformations from Hom_C(A,-) to F are naturally in bijection with F(A). A transformation is determined by its value on the identity of A.

subject: math.CT
name: Co-Yoneda lemma
statement: For a small category C and a covariant functor F:C to Set, the coend of Hom_C(A,X) times F(A), over A in C, is naturally isomorphic to F(X). The coend identifies pairs according to the action of morphisms in C.

subject: math.CT
name: Freyd general adjoint functor theorem
statement: Let C be complete and locally small, D locally small, and U:C to D a functor preserving all small limits. Then U has a left adjoint if, for each object d of D, there is a set of arrows d to U(c_i) through one of which every arrow d to U(c) factors via U of a morphism c_i to c.

subject: math.CT
name: Special adjoint functor theorem
statement: Let C be a complete, locally small, well-powered category with a set of cogenerators, and let D be locally small. A functor U:C to D that preserves all small limits has a left adjoint.

subject: math.CT
name: Beck monadicity theorem
statement: A functor U:D to C with a left adjoint is monadic if it reflects isomorphisms and D has coequalizers of all parallel pairs whose images under U admit split coequalizers, with U preserving those coequalizers. Conversely, every monadic functor satisfies these conditions.

subject: math.CT
name: Uniqueness of adjoints
statement: Any two left adjoints to the same functor are naturally isomorphic, and the isomorphism compatible with the two adjunctions is unique. The dual statement holds for right adjoints.

subject: math.CT
name: Adjoints preserve limits and colimits
statement: A left adjoint preserves every colimit that exists in its domain, and a right adjoint preserves every limit that exists in its domain.

subject: math.CT
name: Pointwise limits and colimits in functor categories
statement: If C is small and D has limits or colimits of a fixed small diagram shape J, then the functor category Fun(C,D) has them as well. Evaluating at any object of C computes those limits or colimits in D.

references.title: Pointwise limits and colimits in functor categories

subject: math.CT
name: Criterion for equivalence of categories
statement: A functor F:C to D is an equivalence of categories if and only if it is fully faithful and essentially surjective, meaning every object of D is isomorphic to an object F(c).

subject: math.CT
name: Mac Lane coherence theorem
statement: Every diagram built from the associativity and unit isomorphisms of a monoidal category commutes whenever its source and target are the same formal tensor expressions. Consequently, reparenthesizing a tensor product gives a uniquely determined canonical isomorphism.

subject: math.CT
name: Strictification of monoidal categories
statement: Every monoidal category is equivalent, by a strong monoidal equivalence, to a strict monoidal category in which associativity and the unit laws hold as equalities.

subject: math.CT
name: Pointwise Kan extension theorem
statement: Let C be small, D locally small, E cocomplete, F:C to E, and K:C to D. The left Kan extension of F along K exists, and its value at d is the colimit of F(c) over pairs (c, K(c) to d) in the comma category (K down d).

subject: math.CT
name: Natural transformations as an end
statement: For functors F,G:C to D with C small and D locally small, the set of natural transformations from F to G is naturally the end over c of Hom_D(F(c),G(c)). The end conditions are exactly the naturality equations.

subject: math.CT
name: Fubini theorem for limits
statement: If C and D are small categories and E is complete, then the limit of a functor C times D to E is canonically isomorphic to either iterated limit, first over C and then D or in the opposite order. The dual statement holds for colimits in a cocomplete category.

subject: math.CT
name: Grothendieck construction theorem
statement: For a small category B, the Grothendieck construction gives a 2-equivalence between pseudofunctors from B opposite to Cat and categories fibered over B with cartesian functors. Choosing cartesian lifts recovers the pseudofunctor from a fibration.

subject: math.CT
name: Freyd-Mitchell embedding theorem
statement: Every small abelian category admits a fully faithful exact functor into the category of left modules over some ring. Exact sequences and their algebraic relations can therefore be studied inside a module category.

subject: math.CT
name: Eilenberg-Watts theorem
statement: An additive right-exact functor from left R-modules to left S-modules that preserves arbitrary direct sums is naturally isomorphic to B tensor_R -, where B is an S-R bimodule. One can take B to be the image of R, with its right R-action induced by right multiplications on R.

subject: math.CT
name: Gabriel-Popescu theorem
statement: Every Grothendieck abelian category is equivalent to the quotient of a module category by a localizing Serre subcategory. Equivalently, it admits a fully faithful right adjoint embedding into a module category whose left adjoint is exact.

subject: math.CT
name: Presheaf topos theorem
statement: For every small category C, the category of functors from C opposite to Set is a Grothendieck topos. In particular, it has all small limits and colimits, exponentials, and a subobject classifier.

subject: math.CT
name: Lambek lemma
statement: If an endofunctor F has an initial algebra a:F(A) to A, then a is an isomorphism. Dually, the structure map of a terminal F-coalgebra is an isomorphism.
